one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-12) contains Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29, before the European open, with the call at 9:30 CET (source 5). Q3 was guided to $3.70B revenue and 37% gross margin, and management already said Q4 would be above $4B (source 2). Alternative data points to a solid quarter: ST pushed price increases in April, June and August 2026 and power lead times run 30-52 weeks (source 7); STM32 lead times were 30-31 weeks at all major distributors (source 8). Against that, the last two reports drew -12% to -15% reactions on guidance (source 15), the stock has derated 39% from its June high while SOXX fell about 16%, and it fell 13% in the last two weeks with the chip sector. The bar is lower than in July. An earnings move of about +/-12% gives fat tails, so the ladder is a near-symmetric lognormal around ~$50 with ~18% one-month vol (61%/3.5 = 17.4%) and a very slight upward tilt for a lowered bar and buybacks still running at ~EUR47 (source 27). No other scheduled company event is in the window. The CEO reappointment (source 4) is neutral.

fair_value.method: Blend of a 10%-WACC DCF ($53.0, 40%) and 17x NTM GAAP P/E on horizon EPS of ~$3.33 ($56.6, 60%), both from the standard engine with consensus-like FY26-27 revenue ($14.4B/$17.3B), a 15.5% GAAP EBIT margin in FY27 and 21% in FY28.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue FY26 $14.43B, FY27 $17.32B, FY28 $18.70B, FY29 $19.45B; GAAP EBIT margin 7.5%/15.5%/21%/21.5%; tax 16%; capex 12-10.5% of revenue; D&A 13.5-10.5%; WACC 10%; g 3%; net cash $1.7B; shares 928M -0.5%/yr

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY26 revenue $14.43B / FY25 $11.80B - 1. Cross-check: Q1 $3.095B + Q2 $3.487B + Q3 guide $3.70B + Q4 'above $4B' = ~$14.3B+.

Consensus FY27 $17.18B (+19.0%); we add ~1pt because ST pushed three price increases in 2026 (TrendForce) and distributor lead times are 30-52 weeks (Findchips, Accuris), and Q4'26 >$4B already annualises to $16B+ before pricing and datacenter (>$2B in 2027 per Q2 release).

Growth slows as the cycle matures; FY28 $18.7B just above the 2023 peak $17.3B (F1). The 2023-25 fall (F1-F3, -32%) after the 2021-22 lead-time spike shows how tight supply tends to end, so we do not extrapolate 20% growth.
H1 GAAP operating income $70M + $187M on $6.58B revenue (3.9%); Q3 gross margin guided to 37% vs 34.8% in Q2, and Q4 above $4B; H2 ~11% gives a full year of ~7.5%.

Consensus FY27 non-GAAP EPS $2.69 x ~925M shares = ~$2.49B net income, which grosses up at a 16% tax rate to ~$2.9B pre-tax, or ~17% of $17.2B; minus ~1.5pts of restructuring and PPA charges that GAAP keeps (Q2: $58M + $24M a quarter) gives 15.5%.

FY2023 GAAP operating margin was 26.7% on $17.3B revenue (F5/F1). We take ~5pts less because D&A is higher (F21 $1,854M vs F19 $1,561M) and Chinese SiC pricing weighs on P&D, partly offset by 2026 price increases.
Effective tax rate was 11.4% in FY23 (541/4,763) and 16.7% in FY24 (313/1,878); FY25 is distorted by low pretax income.
FY25 D&A $1,854M / $11,800M = 15.7%; D&A roughly flat in dollars while revenue grows.
H1 2026 net capex $362M + $409M = $771M, i.e. ~$1.6-1.7B annualised (~11.5% of FY26 revenue); a little more allowed for capacity because lead times are long.
Inventory and receivables move with revenue in a fab-heavy IDM; operating cash flow swings (F27 $5,992M vs F29 $2,152M) show large working-capital effects.
FY25 SBC $193M / $11,800M = 1.6%; included in GAAP EBIT (cost basis).
FY25 buybacks $367M + dividends $321M = $688M; Q2 2026 dividends $75M; buyback still running in Oct 2026 (6-K).
Q2 2026 adjusted net financial position $1.70B (reported NFP $2.01B = $6.03B liquidity - $4.02B financial debt); we use the lower adjusted figure.
Not broken out in the Q2 release; the adjusted net financial position already removes the JV partner's share of cash, and we treat the rest as immaterial.
Q2 2026 weighted average diluted shares 928.0M (FY25 923.1M, F18).
Diluted share count went 944.2M, 939.3M, 923.1M (about -1% a year); a higher share price buys fewer shares with a similar buyback budget.
5.0% risk-free (GS10 4.99%) + ~1.0 beta x 5% premium; net cash balance sheet, so no debt weighting.
Nominal growth for analog/MCU content in autos and industry, below the 2026-27 cyclical growth; FY23-25 history shows how deep the troughs are.

bear.story: Order cycle rolls over in 2027: price hikes and 30-52 week lead times (2021-22 pattern) turn into double-ordering, AI datacenter ramp slips, China SiC pricing hits P&D; revenue growth 6pts lower, margins 4pts lower, P/E 13x.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E (price 2026-10-13 / next-year consensus EPS) 12.4x (NXPI) to 50.7x (SLAB); median 21.7x. Forward EV/EBITDA was not available on a free consensus page; trailing filing-based EV/EBITDA: NXPI 14.5x, ON 20.9x, MCHP 30.9x, ALGM 55.6x, STM 20.9x on trough EBITDA.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM P/E: below the 21.7x median and at the 16.3x median of the closest auto/industrial IDMs (NXPI 12.4x, ON 16.9x, MCHP 18.0x, DIOD 15.6x). STM today is ~18.4x consensus FY27 non-GAAP EPS ($49.57 / $2.69).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the full-peer median holds through the horizon for structural reasons. Margins are lower: FY27 consensus implies ~17% non-GAAP operating margin vs ~40%+ at TXN/ADI. ST is capital-heavy with its own fabs (D&A 15.7% of revenue, F21/F3). Its EV/SiC exposure faces Chinese substrate price cuts (source 13). At the horizon the multiple applies to FY28 earnings near a cyclical high (FY28 revenue above the 2023 peak), and peak earnings historically get lower multiples. We keep a small premium to NXPI for datacenter growth (>$2B in 2027) and a net-cash balance sheet.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$31 (about 11.5x our FY27 GAAP EPS, the bear-scenario value, and back at the March 2026 range before the datacenter re-rating) the market would be pricing a cycle top in 2027, not ordinary volatility. A trade there most likely means one of three things: the 2026 price increases and long lead times turned into double-ordering and cancellations, the >$2B 2027 datacenter target was withdrawn, or margins stalled below ~10% despite revenue near $16B. Any of these breaks the recovery thesis.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine reports that the 17x NTM P/E implies a WACC of about 9.5% on our cash flows (vs our 10%), i.e. the multiple leg is slightly richer than the DCF ($56.6 vs $53.0). With a 10% WACC and 3% terminal growth, the multiple is consistent with a ~21% long-run GAAP EBIT margin and ~4-5% growth after FY2029 continuing a bit longer before fading to 3%. That is plausible but not demanding: ST earned 26.7% in FY2023 on $17.3B revenue (F5/F1). The long-dated risks above (cycle, SiC price war) are why we stop at 21% rather than 2023's 27% and keep the multiple below the 21.7x peer median.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $193M (F25). The model uses GAAP EBIT after SBC. ST's non-GAAP EPS excludes only impairment/restructuring/phase-out costs and NXP MEMS PPA, not SBC (Q2 2026 reconciliation), so consensus EPS is also after SBC. Shares fall only 0.5%/yr net.

reasoning: Start: $49.57, down 39% from the $81.42 June high after the July 23 Q2 report (Q3 guide $3.70B below consensus, EBITDA miss; source 15) and a sector pullback (SOXX about -16% from its June high per the Twelve Data weekly series, a keyed feed so not cited; source 14 attributes earlier weakness to the sector). Fundamentals are recovering fast: revenue +26% y/y in Q2, Q4 guided above $4B, datacenter >$1B in 2026 and >$2B in 2027 (source 2). Consensus is FY26 $14.43B / EPS $1.35 and FY27 $17.18B / EPS $2.69, mean target $75 (source 6). Lane evidence the sell side may underweight: (a) ST raised prices three times in 2026 and power lead times reach 52 weeks (TrendForce, source 7); (b) STM32 lead times are 30-31 weeks at every major distributor (Findchips, source 8); (c) Accuris saw average semiconductor lead times jump 67% in a month to 40 weeks in March 2026 (source 9); (d) blogs note 32-bit MCU/power lead times up to 52 weeks (source 10). This supports near-term revenue and pricing above consensus. But the 2021-22 episode with the same signals ended in a 32% revenue drop in 2023-25 (F1-F3), so we treat it as upside for FY27 and a risk for FY28-29. Community/newsletter sentiment is bullish (Simply Wall St narrative fair value ~EUR67, source 12; Capital Blueprint on the datacenter re-rating, source 11), but it was equally bullish at $81, so it gets little weight. Valuation: engine DCF $53.0 + 17x NTM P/E $56.6, giving $55.2. Scenarios: bear $30.8 (25%), base $55.2 (50%), bull $80.2 (25%). The ladder is a scenario mixture with ~22% within-scenario vol, then tails fattened toward the stock's 61% realized vol: median ~$54, P(>=$50) 56%, P(>=$99) 6%, P(<$30) 14%. Research limits: X/Twitter and Reddit were not reachable (Reddit blocked fetching); Wikipedia pageview data was rate-limited; we found no prediction market on ST-relevant events; Twelve Data estimates/statistics needed a paid plan, so they were skipped. Lane share: peer consensus pages (10) and filings dominate the source count because the peer-set rule requires them; 8 of the 27 sources are in-lane alternative/trade/newsletter/forum sources.
